task.situation:
Your class has carried out an environmental check of your school, and the head teacher would like a report on the results (the figures are invented for this task as a simplified example):
• Energy: the school used 198,000 kWh of electricity in 2026, compared with 180,000 kWh in 2025 (an increase of 10%). After the last lesson of the day, the lights were still on in 14 of the 30 classrooms.
• Waste: in one school week, 350 kg of rubbish ended up in the general waste bins; 140 kg of it (40%) was paper or plastic that could have been recycled.
• Transport: in a survey of 200 students, 124 (62%) come to school by public transport, 40 (20%) walk, 18 (9%) cycle and 18 (9%) come by car. Last year, 26 students came by car.
points: describe the main findings of the check
explain which problems are the most serious
recommend measures the school could take

words.short: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 350 words.

task.de: Report an die Schulleitung. Die Zahlen aus dem Umweltcheck müssen in jedem Abschnitt exakt stimmen. Drei Inhaltspunkte: die Ergebnisse zu Energie, Müll und Schulweg; die größten Probleme; Empfehlungen. Kopf mit To / From / Date / Subject, jeder Abschnitt mit Zwischenüberschrift. Die Zahlen sind für die Aufgabe erfunden.

focus.label: recommendation language
focus.note: Marked: phrases that make a recommendation: should (+ verb), should be + past participle (should be launched) and it would be a good idea to. ‘Could’ for a possibility is not marked.

gaps.q: Our recycling campaign needs a short, catchy name. Two to four words!
gaps.qDe: Gebt der Recycling-Kampagne einen kurzen, einprägsamen englischen Namen (zwei bis vier Wörter), z. B. „Bin it right“.

gaps.q: By what percentage should the school cut its electricity use next year? Shout a realistic number.
gaps.qDe: Um wie viel Prozent soll der Stromverbrauch im nächsten Jahr sinken? Ruft eine realistische Zahl.

steps.q: What is the subject line of our report?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile sagt in wenigen Wörtern, worum es im Report geht.
steps.own: Short and factual: what is the report about?
steps.ownDe: Kurz und sachlich: Worum geht es im Report?

options.label: Name the three areas
options.text: Results of the environmental check: energy, waste and transport
options.why: Factual and precise: the head teacher sees at once which areas the report covers.

options.label: Name the goal
options.text: Making our school greener: findings and recommendations
options.why: States the goal and tells the reader that the report contains findings and recommendations.

steps.q: Introduction: how do we start the report?
steps.de: Die Einleitung nennt den Zweck des Reports und die Herkunft der Zahlen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add the purpose and the data sources in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Zweck und Datenquellen mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add the purpose, the data sources and what the report will do in your own words.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Zweck, Datenquellen und Inhalt des Reports mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.

options.label: Purpose in one sentence
options.text:
### Introduction
In this report we will describe the main findings of the check, explain which problems are the most serious and recommend measures the school could take. The check was about energy, waste and transport, and we asked 200 students.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
In this report we will describe the main findings of the check, explain which problems are the most serious and recommend measures the school could take. The check was about energy, waste and transport. We looked at the electricity bills, weighed the general waste for one week and asked 200 students.
options.reject: This copies the task word for word (‘describe the main findings’, ‘recommend measures the school could take’). State the purpose in your own words.
options.rejectDe: Hier wird die Aufgabe wörtlich abgeschrieben. Den Zweck mit eigenen Worten formulieren.

options.label: Purpose and sources
options.text:
### Introduction
{{This report presents the results of}} our school’s environmental check. {{The figures come from}} the electricity bills, a lights check at the end of the day, a one-week bin check and a survey of 200 students. {{The report also identifies}} the most serious problems and suggests solutions.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{This report presents the results of}} our school’s environmental check. {{The figures come from}} the electricity bills, a lights check at the end of the day, a one-week bin check and a survey of 200 students. {{The report also identifies}} the most serious problems and suggests solutions that the school could put into practice.
options.why: Purpose, data sources and an overview of the report in three clear sentences.

options.label: Start with the aim of the check
options.text:
### Introduction
{{To find out how green our school is,}} our class checked the electricity bills and lights, weighed a week’s general waste and asked 200 students how they travel to school. {{This report presents}} the findings {{and suggests}} improvements.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{To find out how green our school is,}} our class checked the electricity bills for the last two years and counted the classrooms with the lights left on. We also weighed a week’s general waste and asked 200 students how they travel to school. {{This report presents}} the findings {{and suggests}} improvements.
options.why: Explains why and how the data was collected, so the reader can trust the figures.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: what did the check find about energy, waste and transport?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: die Ergebnisse zu Strom, Müll und Schulweg mit den genauen Zahlen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then fill in the figures for electricity, waste and transport.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Zahlen zu Strom, Müll und Schulweg einsetzen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then fill in all the figures for electricity, waste and transport and finish each sentence.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann alle Zahlen zu Strom, Müll und Schulweg einsetzen und jeden Satz fertigschreiben.

options.label: This year compared with last year
options.text:
### Findings
{{First, the electricity bills show that}} the school used 198,000 kWh in 2026, {{10% more than in 2025.}} {{In addition,}} the lights were still on in 14 of the 30 classrooms after the last lesson. {{As for waste,}} 140 kg of the 350 kg in the general waste bins was paper or plastic {{that could have been recycled.}} {{Transport, by contrast, is a strength:}} 82% of students walk or use public transport, and only 9% come by car.
options.textLong:
### Findings
{{First, the electricity bills show that}} the school used 198,000 kWh in 2026, {{10% more than in 2025}} (180,000 kWh). {{In addition,}} the lights were still on in 14 of the 30 classrooms after the last lesson. {{As for waste,}} 350 kg ended up in the general waste bins in one week. {{Two fifths of it}} (140 kg) was paper or plastic {{that could have been recycled.}} {{Transport, by contrast, is a strength:}} 82% of the students walk or use public transport, and only 18 come by car, compared with 26 last year.
options.why: The first sentence names the source and compares the two years; each area then gets its own short part.

options.label: Describe the change
options.text:
### Findings
{{First of all, electricity use rose from}} 180,000 kWh in 2025 to 198,000 kWh in 2026, {{an increase of 10%.}} {{Furthermore,}} the lights were still on after the last lesson in 14 of the 30 classrooms. {{The bin check showed a similar picture:}} 40% of the rubbish in the general waste bins was paper or plastic. {{The transport survey, however, brings good news:}} only 18 of the 200 students come by car, {{down from}} 26 last year.
options.textLong:
### Findings
{{First of all, electricity use rose from}} 180,000 kWh in 2025 to 198,000 kWh in 2026, {{an increase of 10%.}} {{Furthermore,}} the lights were still on after the last lesson in 14 of the 30 classrooms. {{The bin check showed a similar picture:}} 140 kg of the 350 kg in the general waste bins was paper or plastic. {{This means that}} 40% was in the wrong bins. {{The transport survey, however, brings good news:}} 82% of the students walk or use public transport, and only 18 come by car, {{down from}} 26 last year.
options.why: ‘Rose from … to …’ and ‘an increase of’ are the classic phrases for describing a change.

options.label: Change and classrooms
options.text:
### Findings
In 2026 the school needed 198.000 kWh of electricity, a plus of 10% compared to 2025. After the last lesson, 14 from 30 classrooms still had the lights on. Waste is also a problem: 140 kg of the 350 kg in the general waste bins was paper or plastic that could have been recycled. Transport looks much better, as only 18 of the 200 students come by car, eight fewer than last year.
options.textLong:
### Findings
In 2026 the school needed 198.000 kWh of electricity. Compared with 180.000 kWh in 2025, this is a plus of 10%. After the last lesson, 14 from 30 classrooms still had the lights on. Waste is also a problem: in one week, 350 kg of rubbish ended up in the general waste bins, and 140 kg of it was paper or plastic that could have been recycled. Transport looks much better: 82% of the students walk or use public transport, and only 18 come by car, eight fewer than last year.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: a point in large numbers (‘198.000’ → 198,000, as English uses a comma), ‘a plus of 10%’ (→ an increase of 10%) and ‘14 from 30’ (→ 14 of 30).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: 198.000 → 198,000 (Beistrich als Tausendertrennzeichen), a plus of → an increase of, 14 from 30 → 14 of 30.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: which problems are the most serious?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: die ernstesten Probleme. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain in your own words why these problems are serious.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten erklären, warum diese Probleme ernst sind.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain in your own words why these problems are serious and how big they are.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten erklären, warum diese Probleme ernst sind und wie groß sie sind.

options.label: Speak from experience
options.text:
### Main problems
In my opinion, the biggest problem is that some people at our school simply do not care about the environment. Last week, I walked past the empty computer room, and the screens were still on. I often see lights on in empty rooms or full bags of rubbish next to the bins, and I think everybody should just try harder.
options.textLong:
### Main problems
In my opinion, the biggest problem is that some people at our school simply do not care about the environment. Last week, for example, I walked past the empty computer room, and all the screens were still on. I often see lights on in empty rooms or full bags of rubbish next to the bins. Many people also walk past open windows in winter and do nothing about it. I think everybody should just try harder, and then the problems would soon disappear.
options.reject: Personal impressions instead of facts: one walk past the computer room is not a finding, there are no figures, and ‘some people … simply do not care’ is not something the check found. A report bases its judgements on the findings.
options.rejectDe: Persönliche Eindrücke statt Fakten: ein einzelnes Erlebnis, keine Zahlen, und „manche sind gleichgültig“ ist kein Ergebnis des Checks. Ein Report stützt sich auf die Ergebnisse.

options.label: Rank the problems
options.text:
### Main problems
{{Of these findings, wasted electricity is the most serious:}} total use rose by 10% in one year, and lights were left on in almost half of the empty classrooms. {{This costs money and adds to}} the school’s carbon dioxide emissions. {{Second comes}} poor waste sorting, which means that valuable materials end up as rubbish.
options.textLong:
### Main problems
{{Of these findings, wasted electricity is the most serious:}} total use rose by 10% in one year, and lights were left on in almost half of the empty classrooms. {{The extra 18,000 kWh is roughly as much as}} four or five average Austrian households use in a year. {{This costs money and adds to}} the school’s carbon dioxide emissions. {{Second comes}} poor waste sorting, which means that valuable materials end up as rubbish and waste collection becomes more expensive.
options.why: Links back to the findings, ranks the problems and explains why the first one matters.

options.label: Find the common cause
options.text:
### Main problems
{{The two weak results have the same cause:}} everyday habits. Lights stay on in almost half of the empty classrooms, {{while}} paper and plastic too often go into the general waste. {{Both problems are serious because}} they waste money as well as valuable raw materials, and electricity use is still rising.
options.textLong:
### Main problems
{{The two weak results have the same cause:}} everyday habits. Lights stay on in almost half of the empty classrooms, {{while}} paper and plastic too often go into the general waste. {{Both problems are serious because}} they waste money as well as valuable raw materials, and electricity use is still rising. {{The good news is that}} habits are cheap to change: unlike new windows or solar panels, switching off lights and sorting rubbish cost almost nothing and mainly need attention from everyone.
options.why: Picks up the weak results and shows their common cause. This prepares simple, cheap solutions.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: what do we recommend?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: unsere Empfehlungen an die Schulleitung. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own recommendations.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Empfehlungen ergänzen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add your own recommendations and one thing that students can do themselves.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Empfehlungen ergänzen und eine Sache, die Schüler:innen selbst tun können.

options.label: Energy monitors and a campaign
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{Each class [[should]] therefore choose}} two ‘energy monitors’ who check that the lights are off at the end of the day. {{In addition, a campaign called ‘{CAMPAIGN}’ [[should be launched,]]}} and clearly labelled recycling bins [[should be placed]] in every classroom and corridor, so that recyclable rubbish no longer ends up in the general waste.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{Each class [[should]] therefore choose}} two ‘energy monitors’ who check that the lights are off at the end of the day. {{In addition, a campaign called ‘{CAMPAIGN}’ [[should be launched,]]}} and clearly labelled recycling bins [[should be placed]] in every classroom and corridor. As part of the campaign, students could bring reusable bottles and lunch boxes to cut down on plastic waste. {{Finally, [[it would be a good idea to]]}} put a short reminder next to every light switch, so that the last person to leave a classroom switches off the lights.
options.why: ‘Therefore’ links the measures to the problems: one measure for each problem. ‘Should be launched’ and ‘should be placed’ put the action first.

options.label: A target and training
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{The school [[should]] therefore aim to reduce electricity use by {N}%}} next year, for example with automatic light switches in all classrooms and corridors. {{[[It would also be a good idea to]] hold}} a short training session in every class to show students which bin to use for paper, plastic and general waste.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{The school [[should]] therefore aim to reduce electricity use by {N}%}} next year, for example with automatic light switches in all classrooms and corridors. {{[[It would also be a good idea to]] hold}} a short training session in every class to show students which bin to use for paper, plastic and general waste. Small habits such as switching off projectors and computers during breaks also save electricity. {{Class representatives [[should]] remind}} their classmates of these habits once a month.
options.why: ‘Therefore’ links back to the problems, and a clear target makes progress measurable.

options.label: Clear instructions
options.text:
### Recommendations
Teachers, please switch off the lights after the last lesson! Every class must choose two energy monitors, and they must check every room before they go home. Put up posters with the slogan ‘{CAMPAIGN}’ in every corridor and buy clearly labelled recycling bins for all classrooms. Students, stop throwing paper and plastic into the general waste!
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
Teachers, please switch off the lights after the last lesson! Every class must choose two energy monitors, and they must check every room before they go home. Put up posters with the slogan ‘{CAMPAIGN}’ in every corridor and buy clearly labelled recycling bins for all classrooms. The school must also set a target for next year and hold a training session in every class, so that everybody knows which bin to use. Students, stop throwing paper and plastic into the general waste!
options.reject: These are orders, not recommendations: imperatives, exclamations and ‘must’ sound bossy in a formal report to the head teacher. Use should, should be + past participle or it would be a good idea to.
options.rejectDe: Das sind Befehle, keine Empfehlungen: Imperative, Ausrufe und „must“ klingen in einem formellen Report an die Schulleitung zu fordernd. Besser: should, should be + past participle, it would be a good idea to.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end the report?
steps.de: Der Schluss rundet den Report ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the conclusion in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Schluss mit eigenen Worten beenden.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up the strengths and weaknesses and finish the conclusion in your own words.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Stärken und Schwächen zusammenfassen und den Schluss mit eigenen Worten beenden.

options.label: A positive outlook
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{In conclusion,}} our school is already on the right track when it comes to transport. {{The measures for energy and waste [[should be introduced]] soon}} to make our school a model for others.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{In conclusion,}} our school is already on the right track when it comes to transport, as most students travel on foot or by public transport. Electricity use and recycling, however, still need a lot of work. {{The measures for energy and waste [[should be introduced]] soon}} to make our school a model for others.
options.why: Starts with the strength, then calls for action. It ends the report on a motivating note.

options.label: Put it into practice
options.text:
### Conclusion
In conclusion, the recommendations should be put into practice. Our check found that 40 students walk to school and 18 cycle every day. This clearly shows that energy and waste will soon be under control as well.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
In conclusion, the recommendations should be put into practice. Our check found that 40 students walk to school and 18 cycle every day, and only 18 come by car. This clearly shows that the school is on the right track and that energy and waste will soon be under control as well.
options.reject: A conclusion sums up. This one jumps back to figures from the transport survey and draws a conclusion that does not follow: how many students walk or cycle says nothing about energy and waste.
options.rejectDe: Der Schluss fasst zusammen. Dieser springt zu Zahlen aus der Schulweg-Umfrage zurück und zieht daraus einen Schluss, der nicht folgt: Wie viele zu Fuß gehen oder Rad fahren, sagt nichts über Energie und Müll.

options.label: A balanced summary
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{All in all, the picture is mixed.}} {{Although}} transport is a real strength, energy and waste need urgent attention. {{The steps recommended above [[should be taken]]}} before the next school year begins.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{All in all, the picture is mixed.}} {{Although}} transport is a real strength, energy and waste need urgent attention. Fortunately, most of these weaknesses can be fixed quickly, and many of the measures cost very little. {{The steps recommended above [[should be taken]]}} before the next school year begins.
options.why: Sums up strengths and weaknesses and links back to the recommendations.

checks.en: The header has To, From, Date and a clear, factual subject line
Five sections with headings: Introduction, Findings, Main problems, Recommendations, Conclusion
The introduction states the purpose and the sources of the data
All three content points: findings, most serious problems, recommendations
Every figure matches the environmental check
Facts first, then judgements and recommendations
Recommendations use should, should be + past participle or it would be a good idea to
Formal language: no contractions, no personal feelings

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen B1-Report an die Schulleitung mit Kopfzeilen, Zwischenüberschriften und konkreten Empfehlungen. Schwerpunkt sind Wendungen für Empfehlungen (should, should be + past participle, it would be a good idea to); dazu werden Zahlen und Veränderungen korrekt beschrieben (rose, an increase of, two fifths).
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen. Die Zahlen aus dem Umweltcheck an die Tafel schreiben oder als Kopie austeilen, damit alle beim Abstimmen nachrechnen können. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Abschnitt, für „Findings“ (Strom, Müll und Schulweg in einem Abschnitt) 7 min; in der langen Fassung je 2–3 min mehr.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts) und „Report“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Darunter To / From / Date / Subject untereinander wie am Beamer (Date im Report-Kopf: 22 April 2027). Fünf Abschnitte (Introduction, Findings, Main problems, Recommendations, Conclusion); jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile mit seiner Zwischenüberschrift auf einer eigenen Zeile (unterstrichen); am Rand steht nichts. Im Gerüst-Modus werden die Zwischenüberschriften immer mit abgeschrieben. Wendungen für Empfehlungen (should, should be + past participle, it would be a good idea to) grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Zahlen lesen, 2 min Kopf und Betreff, 5 weitere Entscheidungen à ca. 2–3 min (bei „Findings“ die Zahlen kurz nachrechnen lassen), Abschreiben ca. 25 min, 4 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (Doppelstunde): dieselben 6 Entscheidungen, aber längere Abschnitte (Findings ca. 90 Wörter, Main problems und Recommendations je ca. 80, Einleitung und Schluss je ca. 50); Abschreiben ca. 35 min, zusammen ca. 65 min. Die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen und den Beginn der Hausübung nutzen. Gerüst kurz (geplant 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe, 2 min Kopf und Betreff; pro Abschnitt 1 min Entscheidung, realistisch 4–5 min eigenes Schreiben (bei „Findings“ 7 min, dort werden vor allem Zahlen eingesetzt), 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell. In 50 min: beim Schluss nur abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben, den Schluss selbst und die Checkliste als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (Doppelstunde, 100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen; für Findings ca. 9 min, für Main problems und Recommendations je ca. 7–8 min, für Einleitung und Schluss je ca. 5 min eigenes Schreiben, dazu je 1 min Entscheidung und 1 min Vergleich; am Ende 5 min Checkliste.
teacher.traps: Introduction A (LSR): Aufgabe wörtlich abgeschrieben. Findings C (LSA): Punkt statt Beistrich als Tausendertrennzeichen (198.000), a plus of, 14 from 30. Main problems A (TA): persönliche Eindrücke und ein einzelnes Erlebnis (Computerraum) statt Fakten, keine Zahlen aus dem Check. Recommendations C (LSR): Befehle statt Empfehlungen (Imperative, Ausrufe, must), zu fordernd für einen Report an die Schulleitung. Conclusion B (CC): springt zu Zahlen aus der Schulweg-Umfrage zurück und zieht daraus einen Schluss über Energie und Müll, der nicht aus ihnen folgt. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Jede Fassung hat fünf Abschnitte (Einleitung, drei Hauptabschnitte, Schluss). Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen, alle fünf Abschnitte sind darin länger; sie fügt keinen Abschnitt hinzu. Findings bringt die Ergebnisse zu Strom, Müll und Schulweg in einem Abschnitt. Das Datum im Kopf ist fix (22 April 2027), weil der Report die Stromrechnung des ganzen Jahres 2026 auswertet; alle Zahlen sind ein vereinfachtes, erfundenes Beispiel. Bei jeder Zahl im Modelltext kurz nachrechnen lassen (z. B. 198.000 : 180.000 = plus 10 %, 140 von 350 = two fifths bzw. 40 %, 124 + 40 von 200 = 82 %, 18 von 200 = 9 %). Ein durchschnittlicher österreichischer Haushalt verbraucht rund 3.500 bis 4.500 kWh Strom pro Jahr (Main problems, lange Fassung: four or five households). Achtung: Im Englischen steht ein Beistrich als Tausendertrennzeichen (198,000); genau darauf zielt auch die Falle Findings C. Markiert sind nur Empfehlungen; could für eine Möglichkeit bleibt unmarkiert. Die Falle Conclusion B ist als CC eingestuft: Der Schluss folgt nicht aus den genannten Zahlen. Differenzierung: Schnelle formulieren im Gerüst-Modus eine zusätzliche Empfehlung mit should be + past participle. Hausübung: Mini-Report zu einem eigenen kleinen Umweltcheck zu Hause oder in der Klasse (z. B. eine Woche Plastikmüll zählen), mit mindestens drei markierten Empfehlungen.
